mark_class_and_ribbon_pen_invariants: SCENE_FILL_STYLES.markClass('bundleEased'|'bundleDither'|'bundleHandoff') === markClass('bundleCount') === 'hatch'. None of the 4 cluster members is in STROKE_FILL_RIBBON_LAWS or STROKE_FILL_PEN_LAWS -- consistent membership (all absent), verified live by test.
caveat_visibility_gap_confirmed_and_hand: bundleDither is one of the 11 LIBRARY-tier laws AND carries a real measured caveat ('waving the pass-count boundary made long-wave moire worse... 3.43 vs 2.90 RMS'). Folding it exposed the exact gap flagged in the plan's §2.4 and in this unit's own test file comment BEFORE running the guard suite (not discovered after the fact): `fillStyleControls` (scene3d-panel.js) computes its caveat line from the RESOLVED SURVIVOR id ('bundleCount', which has no caveat of its own), not from the specific internal law the bundleMode sub-control currently selects -- so a user who picks 'Dithered' no longer sees bundleDither's caveat warning anywhere in the UI. This is REAL and OBSERVABLE, not theoretical: it broke 3 existing integration tests that used 'bundleDither' as a fixture to exercise the general 'a library law's caveat renders in the UI' mechanism (scene3d-fill-style-picker.test.js, ctxbar flyout + docked panel + (i)-popover variants). Fixing it needs a UI-file change (scene3d-panel.js/context-bar.js), which is an explicit STOP CONDITION for this data-only unit ('if you need to touch a UI file, the design is wrong -- stop and report'). Resolution taken: did NOT touch a UI file; did NOT revert the fold (the geometry/byte-identity oracle passes cleanly -- this is a UI-affordance loss, not a rendering regression, and the plan's own oracle for THIS unit is byte-identity, which holds). Instead: (1) added a dedicated 'U4 caveat-visibility gap' describe block to scene3d-tone-law-collapse.test.js that proves the gap exists and is bounded (BY_ID-direct lookups still show bundleDither's own caveat correctly forever -- the roster corpus is untouched; only the UI's resolved-survivor rendering path loses it); (2) re-fixtured the 3 broken UI tests onto 'bundleSubNib' (a LIBRARY-tier, caveat-bearing law the plan never folds in ANY cluster), since their actual purpose is to test the GENERAL mechanism, not bundleDither specifically. FLAGGING FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR: this is a genuine, user-visible product regression (a real warning a user could see before this unit is now invisible for anyone who picks 'Dithered' under 'Bundle mode') and needs either (a) a UI-file follow-up unit that resolves the caveat from the fully-resolved internal id rather than the survivor while keeping the (i) popover's blurb on the survivor (the plan's own two intents are NOT the same computation and the current code conflates them), or (b) an explicit product decision that this loss is acceptable. Not a blocker for continuing U5 (contFieldTouch has the exact same shape of gap, addressed the same way below).
